name: Plants Per Hectare Calculator
seoTitle: Plants Per Hectare Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: How many plants fit in a field, from the spacing between rows and between plants. Free plants per hectare calculator: enter your values and get space per plan
summary:
How many plants fit in a field, from the spacing between rows and between plants. It returns space per plant, plants per hectare, plants needed and seedlings to buy, and the panel shows all of them at once.

Ten thousand square metres divided by the area each plant occupies gives the population — the number every fertiliser rate, seed order and yield estimate is built on. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Plants Per Hectare
sections.html:
Plants per hectare = 10 000 ÷ (row spacing in m × in-row spacing in m). Total plants = area in ha × plants per hectare × (1 + losses)

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
hahectare, 10 000 m²m²
row spacingdistance between adjacent rowscm
in-row spacingdistance between plants within a rowcm

sections.title: How do I use the Plants Per Hectare?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the area in hectares (1 acre is 0.4047 ha).
  2. Enter the row spacing and the in-row spacing in centimetres.
  3. Add the losses you expect; the plants and seedlings to order are shown.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: area to plant of 1 ha, row spacing of 75 cm, in-row spacing of 30 cm, expected losses of 5%.

Substituting them into the formula gives space per plant of 0.225 m², plants per hectare of 44,444.44 /ha, plants needed of 46,666.67, seedlings to buy of 46,667.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
under 20 000/haWide spacingorchard trees, maize for silage, pumpkins
20 000 – 100 000/haField cropscereals, soybeans, potatoes
over 100 000/haDenseleafy greens, carrots, transplants in beds

  • Spacing sets the population, and population sets the yield curve. Doubling the density does not double the yield, because plants compete for the same light and water.

  • Buy 5–10% more seedlings than the calculated population. Transplant losses and headland waste are real, and a second order mid-season costs more than the surplus.

  • For beds rather than rows, use the bed spacing as the row spacing and count beds per hectare instead of rows.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Mixing centimetres and metres in the same calculation — the classic factor-of-100 error.
  • Forgetting the headland: a 1 ha field with a 3 m headland all round loses about 6% of its plantable area.
  • Planning the population for the seed packet's ideal spacing rather than your equipment's actual row width.

faq.q: How many plants per hectare at 75 × 30 cm?
How do I convert plants per hectare to plants per acre?
faq.a: Multiply by 0.4047, since an acre is 0.4047 ha.

faq.q: Should I add a margin for losses?
faq.a: Yes, 5–10% for field crops and more for transplants or direct-sown small seed.

faq.q: What does the Plants Per Hectare actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns space per plant, plants per hectare, plants needed and seedlings to buy. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
